relations.rationale: Jun being head judge has no bearing on whether Dara and Eli were on different teams.
Being head judge does not imply being the oldest.
Jun being head judge is unrelated to whether Jun set a pace others matched.
Dara's late arrival has no bearing on Eli's height relative to the group.
Dara arriving a few minutes after Esme does not establish that Jun arrived last; someone else could still be later.
Dara being out of breath from jogging is unrelated to Eli's height being useful for spotting markers.
Dara's breathlessness from jogging doesn't indicate anything about Jun's arrival order.
Dara's physical state has no bearing on Yara's age.
Dara's early breathlessness is unrelated to the group's evening tiredness and satisfaction.
Eli being taller than most directly supports the claim that his height made him useful for spotting distant markers.
Eli's height has no bearing on whether Esme and Eli were on different teams.
Eli's height is unrelated to the group's evening rest and satisfaction.
Eli's height has no bearing on the group's readiness to rest.
Eli's usefulness in spotting trail markers is unrelated to Jun's arrival time.
Yara bringing the first-aid kit is unrelated to her tracking time to reach camp before sunset.
Jun arriving last is consistent with and supports the idea that Jun took a wrong turn causing delay.

Jun arriving last contradicts the idea that Jun still made it before the group set off, since arriving last suggests possibly after departure, though it's ambiguous; however 'last' among arrivals could still be before setting off, making it plausible support rather than contradiction.
Taking a wrong turn but still making it before the group set off suggests the delay wasn't too severe, supporting that despite the wrong turn Jun still arrived in time.
Jun's wrong turn near the visitor center is unrelated to the trail's uphill pine forest and meadow description.
Jun's earlier wrong turn is unrelated to the group reaching a rocky outcrop for lunch later.
